SINGURUL LUCRU CARE POATE SALVA ACUM TĂRÂMURILE ESTE UNICUL LUCRU MAI PUTERNIC DECÂT PARCELE.

După uimitoarea trădare ce are drept consecință capturarea de către falsul Rege al Zeilor a Serei și a periculos de seducătorului conducător al Ținuturilor Umbrelor, de care ea este nebunește îndrăgostită, un singur lucru se mai poate face pentru a-l elibera pe Nyktos și a împiedica forțele din Ținuturile Umbrelor să invadeze Dalosul și să stârnească un război între zeii primitivi. Însă Kolis nu poate fi manipulat cu ușurință ‒ nici după o viață întreagă de antrenament în acest sens. În vreme ce Revenantul lui preferat susține cu insistență că Sera nu este nimic mai mult decât o minciună, firea capricioasă a lui Kolis și straniul lui simț al onoarei o zdruncină până în străfunduri pe Sera, pe care nimic nu ar fi putut-o pregăti pentru cruzimile ce au loc la curtea zeului și pentru adevărurile șocante ce îi sunt dezvăluite. Descoperirile acestea nu doar că anulează tot ce credea ea despre propria datorie și despre însuși modul în care au luat naștere tărâmurile, ci pun sub semnul întrebării adevăratul pericol. În orice caz, supraviețuirea în urma confruntării cu Kolis reprezintă doar o parte a luptei. Ascensiunea ei se apropie, și Sera simte cum timpul i se scurge printre degete. Dar Nyktos va face orice pentru a o ține pe Sera vie și a-i oferi viața pe care o merită. Va pune la bătaie însăși distrugerea tărâmurilor – și chiar asta urmează să se întâmple dacă el nu își face ascensiunea ca rege primitiv al vieții. Și totuși, în ciuda determinării lui marcate de disperare, se prea poate ca propriile lor destine să fie mai presus de controlul lui.

La toate astea se adaugă ceva neștiut, nescris și imposibil de prezis. Singurul lucru mai puternic decât Arae...

Jennifer L. Armentrout

jenniferlarmentrout@live.com

# 1 New York Times and # 1 International Bestselling author Jennifer lives in Charles Town, West Virginia. All the rumors you’ve heard about her state aren’t true. When she’s not hard at work writing. she spends her time reading, watching really bad zombie movies, pretending to write, hanging out with her husband and her Jack Russell Loki. In early 2015, Jennifer was diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa, a group of rare genetic disorders that involve a breakdown and death of cells in the retina, eventually resulting in loss of vision, among other complications. Due to this diagnosis, educating people on the varying degrees of blindness has become of passion of hers, right alongside writing, which she plans to do as long as she can.

Her dreams of becoming an author started in algebra class, where she spent most of her time writing short stories….which explains her dismal grades in math. Jennifer writes young adult paranormal, science fiction, fantasy, and contemporary romance. She is published with Tor, HarperCollins Avon and William Morrow, Entangled Teen and Brazen, Disney/Hyperion and Harlequin Teen. Her Wicked Series has been optioned by PassionFlix. Jennifer has won numerous awards, including the 2013 Reviewers Choice Award for Wait for You, the 2015 Editor’s Pick for Fall With Me, and the 2014/2015 Moerser-Jugendbuch- Jury award for Obsidian. Her young adult romantic suspense novel DON’T LOOK BACK was a 2014 nominated Best in Young Adult Fiction by YALSA. Her adult romantic suspense novel TILL DEATH was a Amazon Editor’s Pick and iBook Book of the Month. Her young adult contemporary THE PROBLEM WITH FOREVER is a 2017 RITA Award Winner in Young Adult Fiction. She also writes Adult and New Adult contemporary and paranormal romance under the name J. Lynn. She is published by Entangled Brazen and HarperCollins.

She is the owner of ApollyCon and The Origin Event, the successful annual events that features over hundred bestselling authors in Young Adult, New Adult, and Adult Fiction, panels, parties, and more.

❗️❗️Trigger warnings: captivity, mentions of torture, murder

3.5 stars

Honestly, I liked this one more than I thought I would. After being quite disappointed with A Soul of Ash and Blood, because I thought it was a pointless book and it was way too long for what little it brought to the plot, I was wary of this one, because this series went from being 3 to 4 books sometimes this year and I was dreading another long and pointless filler book. Thankfully, I did like it overall, but many things still annoyed me.

This book picks up right where A Light in the Flame ended. Kolis has Sera, but she manages to convince him that she is Sotoria reborn, even though she doesn’t look like her that much. Nyktos tries to save her, but ends up being beaten by Kolis and Sera and Nyktos then spends about 60% of the book being in a cage. We don’t know much about what happens to Nyktos, but we see every detail of Sera’s daily life in captivity. It’s sad to say, but the most entertaining and interesting parts were when Sera had interactions with Attes, Veses, and Callum. Yeah, you read that right, Veses and Callum were the interesting part of this book, even though they are despicable most of the time and I hate them.

The beginning of the book was engaging and addictive, and I loved it, but then the middle part got repetitive and dragged on, and then I think I was just too bored to truly appreciate the intensity of the last part, so I just found it to be a little mundane and redundant and an excuse to add smut to the book (it was a smut-fest for over 2 chapters). It was cute and romantic, but I was just ready for this book to be over by then to fully enjoy the little crumbles of SeraxNyktos we got.

There were some info-dumps in conversation, as was the case with the other books in this universe, but it wasn’t so bad… At first… It got annoying after a while. I still find it weird though how Attes told Sera that they didn’t have much time to talk, but they then proceeded to have a conversation that lasted for more than 20 pages.

There were still some repetitive conversations and the unending inner monologues of Sera, but the change of setting and the new characters brought some nice changes, thankfully. That being said, I am still beginning to get tired of reading about how brave Sera is. We get it, and we should be able to see it in her actions without the need for the author to write it on every other page.

While I liked seeing more of Attes, I missed the drakens and Ash’s inner circle so much in this book. It felt boring without them around and I really hope they will be more present in the next (and hopefully final?) book. While I’m talking about the characters, wtf was that with Kolis? He has been portrayed as this cruel, cold, cunning, and ruthless Primal since the beginning of the series, but in this book, he mostly appears as an unstable Primal who might need mental help. He just seemed clueless about acceptable social interactions and how to behave with someone you care about, and overall I almost felt bad for him at times because he appeared more like an unstable, sick Primal on a power trip, than a scheming and vindictive one.

I think it would have been refreshing and more engaging to have multiple POVs in this book. I’m getting fed up with Sera’s repetitive inner thoughts, and I would have loved to know more about what Ash thought and went through, even a few Kolis’ chapters would have been a nice and intriguing change.

It was not bad, but again, Sera's inner monologues felt long and repetitive, and there were parts of the story that dragged on, so it was not my favorite book of this series for sure... It could easily have been 100 or 200 pages shorter and still convey everything relevant to the plot and romance.


1. A Shadow in the Ember ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
2. A Light in the Flame ⭐⭐⭐⭐

A guttural, inhuman growl shook the cage.
"Get your fucking hands off my wife."

Spice: 🌶️🌶️🌶️


If I had to describe this book in one sentence it would be 'This is what happens when all-powerful beings don't go to therapy.' Seriously, more than half of these people are in desperate need of professional help. Ironically, I am also in desperate need of a therapist after finishing this book. More accurately, after this book finished me. Thankfully, and this is the only sort of spoiler I'll mention in this review, it doesn't end in a cliffhanger. Quite the opposite, in fact, but that's all I'll say about it.

To begin with, this has been such an intense, gut-wrenching, and wholesome experience. The majority of it is unbearable pain with the briefest moments of relief, and the rest is a compilation of the sweetest, most wonderful moments I've read in this series, so far. There is also entirely too much Kolis in this one, although that was expected, and not nearly enough Nyktos. To be fair, I think Nyktos should be in every scene, on every page, all the time. Alas, that has yet to happen. Unless you count the bonus scene of the last book.

Aside from this rollercoaster of emotions, there are a whole bunch of major revelations for both this series and the original. Revelations that have left me so shooketh, my eyes practically popped out of my sockets. So many things make so much sense now.

Moreover, Sera is absolutely fantastic. She is even more amazing than before. The strength she has is unreal. What she goes through is devastating, yet she is determined to see her plan through. I was so touched by her resilience and determination, and her will to protect those she loves no matter the cost, no matter what happens to her. Equally so, Nyktos is as wonderful as ever. He may not appear as often as I would have liked, at least in the first part of the book, but every moment with him in it is pure bliss. His character arc has some major development of its own, and, as always, his Daddy Nyktos/Dotting Husband vibes are an absolute treat.

Besides, Sera and Nyktos's relationship hit new heights. While many things keep getting between them, they are devoted to each other and determined to stay together at all costs. They share some of the most wholesome and bittersweet moments, and they say the most wonderful things to each other. I lost count of how many times I cried and awed at them. Also, unsurprisingly, they are hot as fuck!

Lastly, you know a book is worth it when the villain is a disgusting, vile filth with an admittedly solid origin story. I hate Kolis with my entire heart. The things he does in this book left me literally nauseous. However, I can admit that his backstory explains perfectly how he turned out to be this way, and that he wasn't always such a horrific person. Yet, none of it is meant to excuse his behavior and actions. It only shows how he turned out the way he did. This sort of villain character arc is one I always appreciate in books.

If you had asked me who my favorite authors were in 2020, JLA would have been at the very top of the list. I have read 30 of her books (yes, I counted), some of them multiple times. She has written some of my all time favorite book boyfriends and I have loved experiencing all of the worlds she has created. I have been a loyal fan for years, but sadly I no longer feel comfortable recommending her work.

This was an absolute turd of a book. It was 632 pages and took place in roughly 8 scenes. There was almost no forward momentum. JLA has lost all sense of timing and no longer seems capable of creating the tension and feeling of urgency needed to keep readers engaged in a story like this. Readers who pick up this book can look forward to spending hundreds of pages trapped in Sera’s repetitive thought spiral. She spends half the book in captivity and the other half having an overly dramatic heart to heart with Ash (read sex) despite the claimed “urgency”of their situation.

I have heard rumors that JLA no longer has an editor and it SHOWS. Girl, you need an editor! This book legitimately should have been 250 pages. There was too much repetition and so much that shouldn’t have made it to print. I am shocked by how highly this book and some of her last books in the Flesh and Fire series are rated. Did we even read the same books? I know it sounds dramatic, but I feel betrayed by her recent works. These beloved characters deserved better and so did her readers. What a disappointment this was. Sigh*

FATES! I HATE KOLIS! HATE!! 🗡️⚔️

"Fire in the Flesh," the third installment in Jennifer L. Armentrout's gripping Flesh and Fire series, continues to captivate readers with the enthralling love story of Ash and Sera. Right from the outset, it's clear that the chemistry between the protagonists is electric, making them a fantasy couple for the ages. Admittedly, personal tastes vary, but for me, their connection has been a highlight since the first book, and this installment only solidifies their status as an ultimate fantasy couple.

What sets this book apart is the depth given to Ash and Sera as individuals. From book one, I've been invested in their characters, and in "Fire in the Flesh," Armentrout not only maintains but surpasses my expectations. The first 50-60% of the narrative is particularly delightful, providing insights into Kolis's motivations and behavior, adding layers to the story.

Quotes:
"Ash was terrifying, his beauty vicious and breathtaking in both forms. And he was mine."

This was super tough to write...I'm a HUGE JLA fan as you can tell from my ratings of all her many books...but I have always tried to be honest in my reviews, and this one should be no exception. This review will contain spoilers so just fair warning!

It was boring. It was frustrating. It was unnecessary! I can't express how disappointed I am. I love the Flesh and Fire series so much, I love Nyktos and Sera so much more than Poppy and Cas and I think this book just may have ruined them for me.

The story picks up right where Light in the Flame left off. Sera manages to convince Kolis that she might actually be Sotoria so after beating the shit out of Nyktos, Solis puts Sera in a lovely cage and there they sit for 65% of this book. I was flabbergasted with all the information. Just continuous questions from Sera, and yes it WAS cute the first two books but this quirk is just magnified by a million and it felt like I was in a lecture hall in college listening to my professor drone on and on. The only parts I felt any type of feeling for was whenever Sera and Callum were bickering and when Veses shows up with her awful self. Imagine that, CALLUM AND VESES saving the book, lol oh my god I laugh to keep from crying! Instead of Kolis being this actual scary villain JLA made him out to just be a creepy, slightly insane guy. At one point you almost feel sorry for him and that almost made me sick to my stomach. He's supposed to be the bad guy!

Finally when Nyktos and Sera get reunited we have to worry about her dying all over again. This part was sad, I admit, but it wasn't enough of a redemption for me to give the book a better rating. Nyktos does his thing and says "Fuck the Fates!" and saves Sera and then they happily fuck for two and a half chapters straight. Look I love JLA's smut usually but this just went on and on and on and on and I found myself skimming. The book ends with them being so in love with each other. That's it. Nothing happened. No amazing cliffhanger to keep me wanting more.

There are so many questions that are STILL unanswered. Is she pregnant yet? There were so many clues through out this book that makes me think she already is, but is it mentioned out right? NO! Other things that bugged me: Why does she have to sleep (in FBAA world), there's no scenes with Jadis or Reaver (UNACCEPTABLE!), what the hell happened to Nyktos? He was written so differently from the first two books in my opinion. First off there's not near enough of him in this book, but I digress. Secondly he seemed so much more soft than from the previous two books almost a weaker waterdowned version of himself. And I'm still stumped on how he was able to love again? If it really is just because they are heartmates and the removal of his Kardia doesn't even matter then what was the whole point?? And him talking of watching Sera grow up....ummmm yeah... that was icky! ALSO, big spoiler here but if Sotoria really is Poppy I will be livid. Don't ruin FBAA like that, I beg!

In my opinion this book wasn't needed. JLA should've kept it to three books and thrown in a chapter or two on what Revenants were. That's basically what we learned here. It was 560 pages of filler. I'm not sure the final book will redeem the series for me. There's still so much that needs to be addressed and I was hoping the timelines would eventually meet up with FBAA but we are still too far from it, I think. Overall super disappointed with this one.

5/5 ⭐️

No surprise here, I enjoyed this one quite a bit. I was worried it would be a filler considering a new book was announced but I really liked this. I enjoyed learning about this world a lot and there’s tons of little hints that I picked up on relating to the FBAA books. I would say a good 50% is learning about those key details, so a lot of information coming at once. At times I felt like it was a little bit slow but other scenes more than make up for it. I got chills when I was connecting certain hints to FBAA and just everything that is revealed.

I wish there were more actual Nyktos and Sera scenes, you’ll understand what I mean when you read it. Sera is such a baddie. I love how she responds to situations. She mostly has no filter and it has me laughing out loud. I love it. She’s so strong and relatable. I love how she has anxiety, I feel like we don’t see this in fantasy books and it felt so real. Also Nyktos is incredible. My heart feels like its being squeezed with how caring he is. I am obsessed with him. He cares so much for Sera. He is adorable and sexy all at once. The shadows? Very hot. I love Sera and Nyktos together. They bicker and argue so often and it’s hilarious. I can’t wait to see where the next book leads and the conclusion to this story.

If you recall how book 2 ended, you know where this one begins. You can also probably guess how that turns out. Long story short (or long story long, in this book’s case), you really don’t see Ash until you’re at the 65% mark. I’m not even kidding. SIXTY-FIVE PERCENT.

What’s going on in the meantime?
1. Sera does a bunch of breathing exercises.
2. Sera drinks a lot of sparkling water. (What was WITH that?! Who cares?!)
3. Kolis wears linen pants.
4. Sera sits there with a whole bunch of power and yet still can’t figure out just ~how~ to get out of this pickle she’s in. I mean wow, what could be the way to fight back? Just WHAT could she do? If only there was someone with a bunch of ALMIGHTY POWER around here who could help.


What really drove me crazy in this book was the complete lack of urgency. Everyone just sort of dicks around when we should be, to quote my grandmother who always yelled at us on Sunday mornings when we were all dragging our feet when putting on dresses for church, getting this show on the road. WHAT IS GOING ON?! We have a lot of pressing matters here, but everyone is just sitting around bantering the same stale lines, in no way concerned about the impending doom of the realms.

This book needed to be no more than 150 pages. I’ll die on that hill (which literally no character will notice because they are busy DRINKING SPARKLING WATER AND FLIPPING THE BIRD).

The keyword for this book is inconsistency. JLA opens Fire in the Flesh with three action packed chapters, that were the best she ever written, and then moves forward to a series of circling and tedious monologues, to pick up again the action, immediately after loosing my interest.

I hardly ever consider DNF a book, and this was a strong candidate for me. I did finish it, but only after pausing it for a bit. Ironically, I’ve paused reading it exactly one page before the return of some sort of plot/ action, which was quite unfortunate.

A Light in the Flame it’s just an info dump to support a new idea for Blood & Ash. If you enjoy that series, you’ll need to read this one before, I don’t see a way around it.

Most of the book was absolutely unnecessary! There are even scenes that were actually good and end up being unnecessary (key to the jail in case some of you have forgotten 🙈). Pages and pages filled with “I’m going to be a white canvas to save Niktos”, “I’m going to behave to save Niktos and make Kolis weak” just to end up infuriating Kolis the second after.
I honestly can’t stand this feisty girl act anymore! It should have been about their love, the angst of saving her despite the lack of Kardia but it takes 63% of the book for them to even be together.

Do you like the secondary characters? I do, but JLA decided they are not important for this book. What is the purpose of creating interest characters and exclude them from a whole book??l

With each new book, the existing characters become more similar with other ones. I’m not sure I can distinguish between Poppy and Sera or Cas and Niktos anylonger. Attes and Nektas read exactly the same to me.

Kolis and Callum were great characters but it was not enough to carry the story.

This book could have been reduced to half its size (probably less) and added the fourth book material to finish the series.

“One of” the reasons we read JLA books it’s the smut, and again, inconsistency is the word here. The smut is absent for most of the book, and when we finally get there, kindle tells me it was 1 hour of it!! I’m a fast reader so for a lot o you it might end up being 2 to 3 hours of only Smut. It was hot, maybe a bit cringe because it was so much of it, but in these chapters we do get what we wanted.

I feel I only do rant reviews now for JLA. Dear Jennifer, please do not attempt to release three books again in the same year. Take your time writing, reviewing, editing.

3 very generous starts because I do love Ash
